scenario.prompt_to_agent:
All Campus 1 PCs (PC5-14) report Campus 2 (10.5.0.x, 10.6.0.x)
is unreachable. Intra-Campus-1 traffic still works. Campus 2
hosts can still reach each other internally. Find the failure
between the campuses.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: mswitch0 ospfd
Mechanism: mswitch0 is Campus 1's multilayer switch — it owns
  the L3 gateways for VLAN 10/20/30 (172.16.10/20/30.254)
  and runs OSPF to advertise these subnets into the backbone.
  Without ospfd, Campus 1 prefixes age out of router16, router7,
  and onward. Campus 2 still has routes intact (their
  advertiser sshswitch/router17 is unaffected) but Campus 1
  becomes invisible.
Localization: mswitch0
Root cause: ospfd not running on mswitch0
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration on mswitch0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on mswitch0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on mswitch0

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ospfd back CONFIG-LESS and the ospf service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ospfd AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration (network statements) on mswitch0. A proposal that restores the missing ospf configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on mswitch0, the Campus 1 multilayer switch that serves as the
Layer-3 default gateway for all VLAN 10 (172.16.10.0/24), VLAN 20
(172.16.20.0/24), and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.0/24) endpoints (PC5–PC14). The
ospfd daemon has been killed and is not running. The /etc/frr/daemons file
marks ospfd=yes, meaning it is intended to run, but the process is absent
from the process table and no frr.conf exists on disk for it to load.

Without ospfd, mswitch0 forms no OSPF adjacency with router16 (which is
directly reachable via the 10.2.2.0/24 segment on br0). As a result,
mswitch0's routing table contains only its four directly-connected prefixes
(10.2.2.0/24, 172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) and no
routes to Campus 2 (10.5.0.0/24, 10.6.0.0/24). When Campus 1 PCs send
traffic toward Campus 2, their packets are forwarded to mswitch0 (the
default gateway), which immediately returns ICMP Destination Net
Unreachable — confirmed by live ping from PC5. Intra-campus traffic works
because those destinations are directly connected on mswitch0. The rest of
the OSPF domain (router16 → router7 → router8 → router17) is healthy and
carries correct bidirectional routes for both campuses; the break is
exclusively at mswitch0's missing OSPF process.

Root cause: ospfd was killed on mswitch0, stripping it of all inter-campus
routing information.

Corrective fix: Restore /etc/frr/frr.conf on mswitch0 with the appropriate
router ospf block (advertising 10.2.2.0/24 and the three VLAN networks into
area 0), then start ospfd (service frr restart or systemctl restart frr).
Once the OSPF adjacency with router16 re-establishes, mswitch0 will learn
routes to Campus 2 and full inter-campus reachability will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names mswitch0 as the device with the fault.
The agent explicitly identifies the ospfd daemon/OSPF on mswitch0 as the failed component and describes its absence and impact.
The agent recommends restoring the FRR OSPF configuration (router ospf/network statements) and restarting the FRR service, which matches the required remediation.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (process list, missing frr.conf, /etc/frr/daemons, mswitch0 routing table, stale LSA, and PC ping unreachable) that support the conclusion that ospfd is not running on mswitch0 and that this causes loss of inter-campus routes. The reasoning chains are logical and the essential alternatives were checked.
